questions.questionText:
Read the following passage and answer the question.

A logistics company installed software that assigns delivery routes automatically. Fuel consumption fell in the first quarter, and drivers reached more addresses each day. The software, however, had no way of knowing that one lane floods after heavy rain or that a particular gate closes at noon. Supervisors began reviewing the generated routes each morning and overriding a handful of them. The combination proved better than either method alone: the software handled the arithmetic of distance while the supervisors contributed knowledge that had never been written down.

Which of the following best describes the theme developed by the author?

options.text: Automated planning works best when it is combined with local human knowledge that the system cannot capture
Route-planning software reduced the company's fuel consumption in the first quarter
Technology has transformed every aspect of modern business
Computers are unsuitable for logistics work

questions.explanationText: The passage shows a routing system succeeding at calculation but failing on local conditions, so humans review its output. The theme must therefore state the general point that holds the whole discussion together, namely that automated planning works best when it is combined with local human knowledge that the system cannot capture. Option 'Route-planning software reduced the company's fuel consumption in the first quarter' is a point that genuinely appears in the passage, but it is a supporting detail rather than the idea the passage as a whole develops. Option 'Technology has transformed every aspect of modern business' is far broader than anything the passage establishes and would fit countless other passages equally well. Option 'Computers are unsuitable for logistics work' runs against the position the author actually takes.

The distortion arises from entirely reasonable individual decisions and belongs to nobody in particular.

A system trained to identify defective castings performed superbly in the factory where its training images had been collected and poorly in a second plant with different lighting. Engineers added images from the new plant, and performance recovered until a third site was added. Each deployment revealed a variation the model had never been shown. Generalisation is not a property a system has; it is a claim about conditions it has encountered.

Which of the following best expresses the theme of the passage?

Computer vision is unsuitable for industrial inspection
Training data should be collected from multiple sites
Performance fell at a plant with different lighting

Option 'Performance fell at a plant with different lighting' is a point that genuinely appears in the passage, but it is a supporting detail rather than the idea the passage as a whole develops.

A plantation of a single fast-growing species was planted to restore a cleared hillside and was counted as forest within five years. Bird surveys found a fraction of the species present in the remaining natural patch nearby, and the soil showed little recovery. Tree cover had been restored and the forest had not. Counting what is easy to count can certify the appearance of a recovery while the thing being recovered is absent.

Which of the following represents the broader idea conveyed by the passage?

options.text: Deforestation is a serious global problem
Restoring an easily measured feature is not the same as restoring the system, though it can certify apparent success
Plantations should never be used in restoration
Bird surveys found fewer species in the plantation

questions.explanationText: The passage shows a single-species plantation counted as restored forest without the ecosystem returning. The theme must therefore state the general point that holds the whole discussion together, namely that restoring an easily measured feature is not the same as restoring the system, though it can certify apparent success. Option 'Deforestation is a serious global problem' is far broader than anything the passage establishes and would fit countless other passages equally well. Option 'Plantations should never be used in restoration' proposes a course of action rather than stating the central idea of the passage. Option 'Bird surveys found fewer species in the plantation' is a point that genuinely appears in the passage, but it is a supporting detail rather than the idea the passage as a whole develops.
